title: Supplementary code for The Sphere Packing Problem in Dimension 4 and the Twenty-Four-Cell Conjecture
description: Programs, certificates, run logs and Lean 4 checks for the paper "The Sphere Packing Problem in Dimension 4 and the Twenty-Four-Cell Conjecture". The paper proves that a Voronoi cell of a packing of unit balls in R^4 has volume at least 8, with equality only for the 24-cell of D_4, at every centre whose neighbours within 2 sqrt 2 all touch it; at every centre with at most twenty-three or at least thirty-one other centres within sqrt 6, or with thirty outside one configuration type; when the twenty-four centres within sqrt 6 lie on the rays of a root system; and when no centre lies strictly between 2 + 4e-26 and sqrt 6. With no assumption on the centres the same cell bounds give density at most 0.63668 for every packing of unit balls in R^4, which is weaker than the three-point bound 0.63611 of Cohn, de Laat and Salmon. The remaining cells are reduced to two explicit statements, (G) and (C), which together would give the optimality of D_4 among all packings and which remain open. The package contains the verification of the certificate of de Laat, Leijenhorst and de Muinck Keizer for twenty-four contacts, with its zonal matrices recomputed in exact arithmetic; the cap inequality for one deviating direction and the region certificates of the arcs; the three-point certificate for twenty-three contacts and its extension to centres at any distance below sqrt 6; the rigidity spectrum of the root system and the explicit constant of the near-contact theorem; the certificate that no 25 points of S^3 have pairwise inner products at most 1/2 + 0.008; the two-point certificates for thirty-one or more centres, the radial counts for twenty-four to thirty and the levels of the density bound; the second-level programme on the enlarged domain; and Lean 4 checks of the finite arithmetic of these steps. Part of the code was developed with the assistance of Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic.
